title: A vendor invoice is due by the vendor's term and recalculated on change
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Your shop enters a bill from a vendor on a term of its own, then changes the bill's date and vendor.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Vendor {Vendor-A} holds the shop's own term {Term-A}, due 14 days after the invoice date, and vendor {Vendor-B} holds Net 30.
    For example: {Vendor-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S7-02 Vendor A, {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S7-02 Fourteen and {Vendor-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S7-02 Vendor B.
  • A vendor invoice {Vendor-invoice-A} for {Vendor-A}, not yet saved, is open in Parts, Vendors, Vendor Invoices.
    For example: {Vendor-invoice-A} is a new vendor invoice for one part.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Set the invoice date to Oct 5, 2026.
  2. Save the vendor invoice.
  3. Change the invoice date to Oct 20, 2026.
  4. Save the vendor invoice.
  5. Change the vendor to {Vendor-B}.
  6. Save the vendor invoice.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the due date shows Oct 19, 2026 (Oct 5 + 14 days).
  • Step 2: it is saved with due date Oct 19, 2026.
  • Step 3: the due date is recalculated to Nov 3, 2026 (Oct 20 + 14 days).
  • Step 4: it is saved with due date Nov 3, 2026.
  • Step 5: the due date is recalculated to Nov 19, 2026 (Oct 20 + 30 days, Net 30).
  • Step 6: the stored due date is Nov 19, 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-R9: “A vendor invoice stores no term. Its due date is calculated by the same rules from the vendor's term when the vendor invoice is created, recalculated when its invoice date or its vendor changes, and stored.”
  • S7-R1: “A Net term (standard or the shop's own) is due that many days after the invoice date: an invoice dated Oct 5 on Net 30 is due Nov 4; on a shop's "Net 10" it is due Oct 15.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
